mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare the joint ratio of goals-FOR to shots-FOR (and goals-FOR to shots_on_target-FOR) in the ALL_PRIOR window versus the RECENT_5 window for Team A. The mechanism tests whether a recent spike in shots is accompanied by a commensurate rise in goals, or whether the two observables diverge — a non-linear / saturation relationship not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's recent shots spike is expected to show diminishing returns in goals relative to the all-prior baseline, i.e. goals-per-shot ratio falls as shot volume rises
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has surged in recent matches while its conversion rate (goals per shot) has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot production and scoring efficiency. Jointly measuring shots FOR and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows reveals whether elevated shot counts translate into proportionally elevated goals, or whether the relationship saturates/decouples.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and goals) across two time windows simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band; the engine would need to evaluate the ratio of two observables and whether that ratio changes across windows.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For Team B, compute the joint relationship between shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST in the ALL_PRIOR window versus the RECENT_5 window. The mechanism tests whether the recent rise in shots conceded is accompanied by a disproportionate rise in goals conceded (implying a quality/conversion shift) or a proportionate one (implying a volume shift only).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In Team B's recent matches, goals conceded rises faster than shots_on_target conceded relative to the all-prior baseline, indicating a worsening shot-to-goal conversion rate against them beyond what shot volume alone explains
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's defensive solidity (shots conceded) has deteriorated sharply in recent matches while its goals-against has also risen, but the two observables move at different rates. Jointly tracking shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST across all-prior versus recent-5 windows tests whether Team B's recent defensive breakdown is driven by volume of shots allowed, quality of shots allowed, or both simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires joint evaluation of two distinct defensive observables (shots_on_target AGAINST and goals AGAINST) and their ratio across two time windows — not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's corners FOR (all-prior and recent-5) and Team B's corners AGAINST (all-prior and recent-5) simultaneously, testing whether the combination of a stable attacker and a recently-leaky defender produces a corner total that diverges from what either team's individual baseline would suggest. This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint pairing of Team A's stable corner production with Team B's sharply elevated recent corners-conceded rate is associated with a higher corner total than either team's own all-prior average would predict in isolation
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kicks conceded have spiked dramatically in recent matches (8.4 recent vs 5.1 all-prior) while Team A's corner kicks earned are stable. This asymmetric divergence between Team B's recent corners-against and Team A's corners-for suggests a structural mismatch: the joint combination of Team A's corner production rate and Team B's corner-concession rate in recent form may predict a corner total that neither observable alone would indicate.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: it pairs one team's FOR observable with the opponent's AGAINST observable and explicitly tests whether the recent-form divergence between the two (one stable, one spiking) creates a non-additive signal. The engine's mirror covers same-observable FOR vs AGAINST symmetrically; this tests the asymmetric divergence in recent-form trajectories jointly.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For both teams, jointly compare cards_2h (second-half period) FOR and AGAINST against full-match yellow_cards FOR and AGAINST, and against the competition cards_2h baseline. The mechanism tests whether the within-match temporal distribution of cards (first half vs second half) is consistent with a uniform distribution or whether cards concentrate in the second half — a within-match state dependence requiring half-level resolution.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Cards concentrate disproportionately in the second half relative to a uniform within-match distribution, and this concentration is more pronounced when both teams have elevated second-half card rates relative to their full-match averages
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards rate and Team B's second-half cards rate differ from their respective full-match yellow card rates in ways that suggest the second half of this fixture may have a distinct disciplinary profile. Jointly measuring each team's cards_2h (second-half cards FOR and AGAINST) against their full-match yellow_cards and the competition's cards_2h baseline tests whether the second half concentrates disciplinary events beyond what the full-match rate implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires within-match half-level resolution (cards_2h vs full-match yellow_cards) and a joint cross-team comparison of second-half disciplinary rates against the competition baseline — not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's offsides AGAINST (recent-5 vs all-prior) and Team B's offsides FOR (recent-5 vs all-prior), further conditioning on possession to assess whether the offside pattern is consistent with Team B's possession profile. The mechanism tests whether the two observables move in opposite directions simultaneously — an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship — and whether possession mediates this divergence.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's offsides-against rate spikes while Team B's offsides-for rate drops simultaneously, the joint signal diverges from what either team's individual baseline predicts, suggesting a structural mismatch in attacking depth versus defensive line positioning that is not captured by either observable alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's offsides conceded (AGAINST) have spiked sharply in recent matches (4.2 recent vs 2.0 all-prior) while Team B's offsides FOR have dropped (0.8 recent vs 1.9 all-prior). This creates a cross-team asymmetric divergence in the offsides dimension: one team is suddenly generating far more offsides traps while the opponent is running fewer offside-risk attacking movements. Jointly measuring Team A's offsides AGAINST and Team B's offsides FOR across all-prior and recent-5 windows tests whether this divergence reflects a structural tactical shift in how the two teams interact.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly evaluating two distinct observables (offsides and possession) across two teams in opposite directions simultaneously — an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship across two observable dimensions, not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.
